card.statement:
Our proof of Theorem 1.7 shows that all the representative ind-schemes involved are actually ind-almost reduced i.e. can be expressed as colimits of almost reduced affine schemes, where an affine scheme $\mathrm{Spec}\,A$ is almost reduced if the nilradical of $A$ is nilpotent.

1.2.2. Reduction to the case of the multiplicative group

The proof of Theorem 1.7 and of Lemma 1.2 reduces to the case of the multiplicative group. In this section we assume the results true for $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ and we deduce the results for any solvable group.

We start by remarking that Theorem 1.7, and Lemma 1.2 are easily verified in the case of $G=\mathbb{G}_{a}$ . In fact, for Lemma 1.2 it is enough to take $\Sigma_{G}(R)=tR[t^{-1}]$ , while Theorem 1.7 is a consequence of the following lemma.
card.label: Remark 1.8

paper.title: Two dimensional versions of the affine Grassmannian and their geometric description
paper.abstract: For a smooth affine algebraic group $G$ over an algebraically closed field, we consider several two-variables generalizations of the affine Grassmannian $G(\!(t)\!)/G[\![t]\!]$, given by quotients of the double loop group $G(\!(x)\!)(\!(y)\!)$. We prove that they are representable by ind-schemes if $G$ is solvable. Given a smooth surface $X$ and a flag of subschemes of $X$, we provide a geometric interpretation of the two-variables Grassmannians, in terms of bundles and trivialisation data defined on appropriate loci in $X$, which depend on the flag.
